general_information.Description: This course provides a comprehensive understanding of the evolution, transformation, and future directions of the Hospitality and Tourism industries. It highlights the interconnectedness between traditional issues—such as overtourism, crisis management, destination recovery, and the sharing economy—and emerging innovations driven by Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data, and sustainable practices. Students will explore how these forces collectively shape management, marketing, and service delivery, as well as their ethical and social implications. Key themes include environmental sustainability, digital transformation, AI in guest experience design, and data-driven decision-making. Throughout the course, students will engage with AI-based platforms (e.g., ChatGPT, Perplexity AI, Excel Copilot, and Beautiful.ai) to conduct research, analyse data, and present findings through interactive formats. The course emphasizes experiential learning, collaboration, and critical reflection, helping students bridge theory and practice to develop adaptive and future-ready competencies in the global hospitality landscape.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to http://flm.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information>
general_information.Tools: Internet sources & AI tools ( Students are encouraged to use, Notion AI, SciSpace, and Elicit for self-study, concept explanation, and summarizing trends. For data analysis in hospitality, tools like Excel Copilot, Wolfram Alpha, and ChatGPT Code Interpreter help visualize industry statistics.)
general_information.Note: Academic journals (https://www.tandfonline.com): Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Technology, International Journal of Hospitality Management, International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management, Tourism Management, Journal of Sustainable Tourism, Current Issues in Tourism, Tourism Review, Annals of Tourism Research, International Journal of Tourism Cities, Journal of Destination Marketing & Management. Online resources: https://www.unwto.org http://www.leisuretourism.com/ https://www.cabi.org https://www.globalwellnesssummit.com https://wttc.org

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Research, identify and describe the comtempory issues of tourism and hospitality
Interpret, discuss and debat the issues with their own arguments
Select, evaluate reference materials and incorporate them appropriately into group work
Convey understandable information to the audience and convince them with logical reasoning
Organize interesting activities to convey ideas and concepts
Develop independent thinking, analytical capacity and eloquence
Develop brainstorming, communication, responsibility in team corporation.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: The presentation must cover a specific aspect of the topic mentioned and demonstrate the integration of AI tools (such as ChatGPT, Canva AI, Gemini, Copilot, etc.) to support content creation, data analysis, visualization, or idea development. Option 2 (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal, encouraging students to apply AI-assisted exploration and reflection as part of their constructivist learning process.
assessments.Grading Guide: Option 1: For each topic, each group (4–6 students) will choose an aspect to introduce in different forms such as presentation, case study, workshop, discussion, quiz, games (crossword puzzles, Q&A..), role play... to convey knowledge to other groups in the class. Students are encouraged to integrate AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Canva AI, Gemini, Copilot, or other generative AI applications) to support research, idea generation, content creation, visual design, data visualization, or simulation activities during preparation and presentation. With controversial topics, teams can conduct a 1–1 debate on an issue, optionally using AI to simulate arguments, gather contrasting perspectives, or analyze bias. Each topic lasts 3–4 slots: Slot 1: General understanding of topics and topic selection by groups. Slot 2: Groups work, discuss, and use AI tools for research and content development. Slots 3–4: Group presentations and peer learning. Scoring recommended (see evaluation forms): 50% by lecturer (50% group, 50% individual) 50% by other groups Option 2 (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal, with an emphasis on AI-assisted exploration and reflection, where students co-construct knowledge using digital and AI-supported inquiry tools.

Class preparation and pre-reading before lecture will be assessed upon individuals' understanding and ability to answer questions in the class. Individuals will be called up randomly to be assessed. assessments.Grading Guide: The final exam accounts for 30% of the total grade, consisting of multiple-choice questions that assess students’ comprehensive understanding of all course topics. It covers both traditional issues (overtourism, crisis management, recovery, sharing economy) and emerging trends (AI, Big Data, sustainability, innovation, and digital transformation) shaping the future of the hospitality and tourism industry.
